answer: In a sponsorship graph, each audited root owns a fixed admission budget. Every downstream terrace inherits a share; it cannot mint new capacity. A wharf contract admits an agent only by locking one budget slot plus an onyx bond from its sponsor until random fraud audits finish. Splitting into 1,000 aliases still requires 1,000 scarce slots; proven common-control fraud burns the bond. This bounds farms by root capacity, but depends on honest root audits and appeals.
